subject: Materials Science
title: Transparent Conducting Oxides
description: A micro-lesson that makes Transparent Conducting Oxides usable.

hook.text: Your phone screen is coated with a material that is both transparent and electrically conductive.

buildup.text: Indium tin oxide lets light through while carrying the current that controls each pixel.

discovery.text: A wide band gap means visible light passes, while heavy doping provides free carriers for conduction.

twist.text: Indium is rare and expensive — researchers race to replace ITO with aluminum-doped zinc oxide.

climax.text: Every touchscreen, OLED display, and thin-film solar cell depends on transparent conductors.

punchline.text: A material that conducts yet lets light pass — the invisible wire.

quiz.question: Why are transparent conducting oxides transparent?
options: They are extremely thin and flexible
Their wide band gap prevents absorption of visible light
